info.title: CW Ticket Tools v6
info.description: Tools for counting, searching, and retrieving notes from ConnectWise Manage tickets.

BearerAuth.name: Authorization
BearerAuth.description: Enter the API token as "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN".

post.description: Counts ConnectWise Manage tickets using a semantic request body. Use this tool for questions asking how many, count, number of, total, or quantity of tickets match conditions. Build the where array only from filters stated or strongly implied by the user. Do not ask for filters that are not mentioned. Use entity ticket. For company, customer, account, organization, client, or site names, use field company with operator contains. For text in the ticket summary, use field summary with operator contains. For multiple words or phrases that all need to appear in the ticket summary, use field summary with operator contains_all and an array of strings. For status or lifecycle terms, use field status with operator semantic_eq. For board names, use field board with operator contains. For owner names, use field owner with operator contains. For entered or updated date ranges, use date_entered or last_updated with gte and lte operators.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: Semantic ticket count request. Use entity ticket. Include a where array containing only the filters needed to answer the user's question. Omit unused filters.

post.description: Searches ConnectWise Manage tickets using semantic field names. Use this for prompts asking to find, show, list, or retrieve tickets. For count questions, use Count ConnectWise tickets instead. Build the where array only from filters stated or strongly implied by the user. Do not ask for filters that are not mentioned. Use entity ticket.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: Ticket search request containing entity, filters, selected fields, ordering, and row limit.

post.description: Retrieves structured ticket notes for tickets matching semantic ticket filters. Use this only when the user asks to summarize, synthesize, review, explain, inspect, or read ticket notes. Do not use this tool for count questions. Build ticket_where only from filters stated or strongly implied by the user. Do not ask for filters that are not mentioned.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: Ticket notes request containing ticket filters and note limits.

SemanticFilterCondition.description: A single semantic filter condition for ticket search, ticket count, or ticket note requests. Only create filters for conditions the user stated or strongly implied.

field.description: Semantic ticket field name. Use company for company, customer, account, organization, client, or site names. Use summary for text in the ticket summary. Use status for status or lifecycle terms. Use board for board names. Use owner for ticket owner names. Use date_entered for ticket entered dates. Use last_updated for ticket updated dates.

operator.description: Filter operator. Use contains for simple text matching. Use contains_all when several words or phrases should all appear somewhere in the same field. Use contains_any when any one of several words or phrases can appear. Use semantic_eq for lifecycle status terms like open, closed, completed, done, active, inactive, scheduled, waiting_client, and waiting_vendor. Use gte and lte for date ranges.

value.description: Filter value. For contains_all and contains_any, use an array of strings when possible. For most other operators, use a string, number, boolean, or list as appropriate.

SemanticTicketCountRequest.description: Request body for counting ConnectWise Manage tickets. Always use entity ticket. The where array is required and must contain only the filters needed to answer the user's question. Do not ask for filters that are not mentioned.

entity.description: The entity being counted. Always use ticket.

where.description: Filters to apply to the ticket count. Include only filters explicitly stated or strongly implied by the user. For "How many Oaklawn tickets have SentinelOne in the summary?", use two filters: company contains Oaklawn, and summary contains SentinelOne.

SemanticOrderBy.description: Sort instruction for ticket search results.

direction.description: Sort direction. Use asc or desc.

SemanticSearchRequest.description: Request body for searching ConnectWise Manage tickets. Use entity ticket. Include only filters that are needed to answer the user's question. Do not ask the user for optional filters that were not mentioned.

entity.description: The entity being searched. Always use ticket.

select.description: Optional list of ticket fields to return.

where.description: Semantic filters to apply to the ticket query. Include only filters explicitly stated or strongly implied by the user. Omit unused filters.

include.description: Optional includes. Usually omit because includes are inferred from selected and filtered fields.

order_by.description: Optional sort instructions for ticket search results.

limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return.

SemanticSearchResponse.description: Ticket search response containing matching ticket rows.

entity.description: The entity returned by the API. For this tool, this should be ticket.

columns.description: Names of the fields returned in each ticket row.

rows.description: Matching ticket records returned by the API.

entity.description: The entity returned by the API. For this tool, this should be ticket.

TicketNotesRequest.description: Request body for retrieving notes from matching tickets. Include only ticket filters that are explicitly stated or strongly implied by the user.

ticket_where.description: Filters used to find matching tickets before retrieving notes. Include only filters explicitly stated or strongly implied by the user. Omit unused filters.

limit_tickets.description: Maximum number of matching tickets to collect notes from.

limit_notes.description: Maximum number of notes to return.

include_internal.description: Whether to include internal analysis and internal member notes.

TicketNotesResponse.description: Ticket notes response containing structured notes from matching tickets.

columns.description: Names of the fields returned in each ticket note row.

rows.description: Matching ticket note records returned by the API.
